Hi all — tagging in from Tax Ops. Thanks for the context, Connor and Ana. For EIN reconciliation we accept one of the following (in order of preference):

1) Bank letter on official bank letterhead referencing the company name and account details (scan with bank stamp) — fastest for our review team
2) Officer attestation (signed by C-level or Finance head) that explicitly states the EIN and signer authorization
3) Notarized W-9 if we have reason to suspect the signature is not an authorized company signatory

If the W-9 and bank letter show different EINs, we need a short attestation explaining the discrepancy (e.g., acquisition, DBA vs. legal entity) plus supporting docs (acquisition agreement, DBA filing, etc.). If Fulcrum recently changed legal name or spun a subsidiary, that often explains a mismatch.

Ana — please upload the bank letter or your officer attestation to the intake portal Connor linked. If you prefer DocuSign, send the envelope link and we will accept the audit trail as evidence. Once we have either the bank letter or attestation, Tax Ops will complete the EIN verification within one business day and push the vendor record through procurement.

Procurement checklist we will follow after verification:
- Confirm legal entity matches invoice remit-to
- Confirm EIN/TIN match or reconcile with supporting docs
- Set vendor terms and create PO number in Coupa

Reference: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PROC-8421

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
